primitives.name: Real Value Ladder
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Real value ladder** — Free "understand how Galaxy thinks" / Pro "read today's board with confidence" / Elite "understand the market behind the board" / Operator "run a serious workflow." Each: plain-English promise, who it's for, what unlocks, what stays gated, why the next tier exists.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'V': 'value tier level (dimensionless)', 'U': 'user cohort identifier (categorical)', 'F': 'feature set (set of features)', 'G': 'gate status (boolean)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each tier provides increasing information gain relative to previous tier; user selects based on marginal utility maximization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: V(n+1) > V(n); F(n+1) \subset F(n); G(n+1) = true implies G(n) = false

layer2.mapping: Each value tier maps to a conditional entropy reduction in user decision space, where V(n) = H(U|F(n)) - H(U|F(n-1))
layer2.telemetry: User conversion rate between tiers, feature unlock frequency

primitives.name: Feature Gating System
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Feature gating system** — each feature: key, display name, plain-English explanation, internal description, plan availability, status (live/demo/ preview/waitlist/planned/disabled), data-readiness, proof requirement, compliance risk, value score, competitor analog, UI lock behavior, upgrade CTA.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_k': 'feature key (string)', 'P_a': 'plan availability (set of plan IDs)', 'S': 'status (live/demo/preview/waitlist/planned/disabled)', 'R': 'risk score (real, 0–1)', 'V_s': 'value score (real, 0–1)', 'C': 'compliance risk (boolean)'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are independently gated by plan tier; risk and value scores are monotonic with respect to feature maturity.
primitives.breakdown_regime: S = live ⇒ P_a ⊆ {Pro, Elite, Operator}; R < 0.5 ⇒ C = false

layer2.mapping: Feature gating defines a kernel over feature-space that partitions user access based on plan tier and risk threshold; kernel k(F_i, F_j) = 1 if both accessible under same plan, else 0
layer2.telemetry: Feature unlock rate, upgrade CTA click-through, compliance violation count

primitives.name: Pricing Page Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Pricing page** — hero 10s value prop, trust subhead, plan cards, comparison matrix, "What Free includes/excludes," "Why Galaxy gates picks," "How confidence works," "What No-Bet means," proof/calibration, founding/promo, FAQ, responsible-gaming footer, mobile-first, accessible locked states.
primitives.assumptions: User evaluates plans in parallel; trust signals increase perceived value; locked states must be clearly communicated.
primitives.breakdown_regime: T ≥ 0.7 ⇒ L_s = false; C_m[i][j] = 1 iff feature i available in plan j

layer2.mapping: Pricing page structure mirrors a decision tree over user preference space; T represents posterior belief in plan quality given evidence
layer2.telemetry: Plan card view duration, comparison matrix interaction, locked state click-through rate

reasoning_traces.think:
The value ladder encodes a hierarchical Bayesian model of user information processing, where each tier corresponds to a posterior belief update conditioned on prior knowledge and feature access. The feature gating system acts as a probabilistic filter, assigning risk-adjusted access to features based on plan tier and compliance constraints. The pricing page functions as a structured communication protocol, encoding trust signals and comparative value propositions to guide user choice. Together, these primitives define a closed-loop system of value delivery, where user feedback loops into dynamic pricing and feature allocation. Failure modes include misalignment between perceived and actual value, over-gating leading to churn, and under-gating causing compliance risk. The system's robustness depends on continuous calibration of feature value scores against user engagement metrics.
